handoff.purpose: Render tier2, gate, and combined report strings from result dicts.

symbols.name: render_tier2
symbols.note: Formats tier2 result dict into a string; handles skipped, per-task table, aggregate, truncation warnings, errored tasks.

symbols.name: render_gate
symbols.note: Formats gate result dict into a string; handles pass/fail, regressions, improved, new, missing, errored primary/quarantine, focus-withheld, and update-baseline hint.

symbols.name: render
symbols.note: Concatenates render_tier1, render_arms (if arms given), and render_tier2 (if tier2 given).

claims.text: ADVISORY regression-ratchet report -- see harness.run_gate docstring. This never blocks anything by itself; it is a local developer command.
claims.why: The claim that render_gate never blocks is a property of the caller (harness.run_gate), not of this function; this chunk only builds a string.

claims.text: errored tasks ... SKIPPED (not counted in the aggregate above)
claims.why: The aggregate line (lines 297-299) uses result['success_A']/result['n_tasks'] and result['success_B']/result['n_tasks']; errored tasks are only appended in a separate section after the aggregate, so they are not counted in that aggregate.

claims.text: TOK_B is what was actually sent to the model (may be truncated to fit the context window); TOK_B(true) is the real, untruncated whole-repo size.
claims.why: The header row uses t['tokens_B'] for TOK_B and t.get('tokens_B_true', t['tokens_B']) for TOK_B(true), and the aggregate line distinguishes B (sent) = result['tokens_B'] from B (true, untruncated) = result.get('tokens_B_true', tok_b).

claims.text: WARNING: B was TRUNCATED to fit the model's context window for at least one task -- B (sent) above understates the real whole-repo baseline; a truncated baseline is a WEAKER one, not a fair comparison.
claims.why: The warning is emitted only when result.get('b_truncated_any') is truthy, and it states that B (sent) understates the real baseline.

claims.text: Errored tasks (result.get: absent for any hand-built pre-existing gate result dict, and always absent -> no lines added when there are none).
claims.why: The code uses result.get("errored_primary") or [] and result.get("errored_quarantine") or [], so absent keys yield empty lists and no lines are added.

claims.text: Focus-withheld tasks (result.get: absent for any hand-built pre-existing gate result dict) -- a fence fail-closing on a task's own focus file is NOT a recall regression (see harness.run_gate); reported here, never folded into REGRESSIONS above.
claims.why: focus_withheld is read via result.get("focus_withheld") or [] and rendered in its own section, separate from the REGRESSIONS section; the claim that it is never folded into REGRESSIONS is upheld by the code.

claims.text: No primary-tier task lost recall vs the stored baseline.
claims.why: This line is appended only when not result["regressions"] and not errored_primary, which matches the claim.

claims.text: Run 'python -m daedalus.eval --update-baseline' to intentionally accept the current numbers as the new baseline (explicit only, never automatic).
claims.why: The claim that the baseline update is explicit-only and never automatic is a property of the CLI/harness, not of this rendering function; this chunk only prints the hint.

observations.what: render_gate's banner is PASS/FAIL based solely on result['passed']; the docstring says it never blocks, but the banner itself does not encode any blocking logic.
render_tier2 assumes result['per_task'] exists and is iterable when not skipped; no guard for missing keys.
render_tier2 assumes result['provider'] has 'kind', 'model', 'host'; missing keys would raise KeyError.
render_tier2 assumes result['n_tasks'], result['success_A'], result['success_B'], result['tokens_A'], result['tokens_B'] exist; missing keys would raise KeyError.

render_gate assumes result['passed'], result['baseline_path'], result['n_checked'], result['regressions'], result['improved'], result['new_tasks'], result['missing_tasks'] exist; missing keys would raise KeyError.

render_gate's 'No primary-tier task lost recall' line is only shown when there are no regressions and no errored_primary; but it does not mention whether the gate passed/failed overall -- a FAIL due to errored_primary still shows this reassuring line if regressions are empty.
render_tier2's ratio is computed as 100 * tok_a / tok_b; if tok_b is 0, it shows 'n/a' but the aggregate line still prints both token counts without flagging the zero denominator.
render_gate's focus_withheld section does not show the reason for withholding, only the id and target.

risks: render_tier2 | medium | Missing keys in result dict will raise KeyError, breaking the report | Add guards or document required keys
render_gate | medium | Missing keys in result dict will raise KeyError, breaking the report | Add guards or document required keys
render_gate | medium | 'No primary-tier task lost recall' line may appear even when gate FAILs due to errored_primary | Check whether the line should be conditional on result['passed']
render_tier2 | low | Zero denominator in ratio leads to 'n/a' but no explicit warning | Consider adding a warning when tok_b is 0
